repairs.title: Directory identity: AD DS and AD FS do different jobs

sections.heading: Directory objects
sections.text: Active Directory Domain Services stores users, computers, groups and other domain objects. Domain controllers serve the domain; trees and forests define directory structure and trust boundaries.

sections.heading: Federation across applications
sections.text: AD FS is a federation service that can authenticate a corporate user and issue a SAML assertion for application sign-in. An assertion is not an AWS access key.

sections.heading: AWS access follows trust
sections.text: For AWS federation, configure the identity-provider and role trust, then obtain the intended AWS session. Directory trust, SAML federation and AWS permission policies are separate controls.

repairs.remember: A directory stores identities; federation carries an authentication claim across a trust boundary.
repairs.layout: Module09 style; named teaching sections with clean functional service illustrations

repairs.title: Choose Managed Microsoft AD, AD Connector or Simple AD

sections.heading: Managed Microsoft AD
sections.text: A managed Microsoft directory in AWS supports traditional AD-aware workloads and supported trusts/integrations. AWS operates domain controllers; you still manage users, groups and application permissions.

sections.heading: AD Connector
sections.text: A gateway forwards supported directory requests to an existing AD. Users remain in that directory; connectivity and directory availability matter. It is not a replica or an offline credential cache.

sections.heading: Simple AD
sections.text: A standalone Samba-based directory supports basic compatible domain/LDAP workflows. It lacks forest trusts, MFA and full Microsoft AD feature compatibility; verify application support before selection.

repairs.remember: Choose by required directory features and failure dependencies, not by a generic SSO label.
repairs.layout: Module09 style; named teaching sections with clean functional service illustrations

repairs.title: Managed Microsoft AD: availability, sharing and integrations

sections.heading: Operate across AZs
sections.text: Managed domain controllers are deployed across two AZs; supported scaling and backups protect directory operations. Directory resilience does not automatically make each dependent application resilient.

sections.heading: Connect compatible workloads
sections.text: Windows domain join, supported RDS SQL Server, virtual desktops and traditional AD applications require the right directory, DNS and network paths. Share supported directories across eligible accounts/VPCs.

sections.heading: Extend across Regions
sections.text: Supported Multi-Region replication extends managed directory availability. Its behavior differs from a forest trust or a self-managed replica; verify supported integrations and regional MFA constraints.

repairs.remember: Directory availability, workload compatibility and access permissions must be designed together.
repairs.layout: Module09 style; named teaching sections with clean functional service illustrations

repairs.title: Trust and replication preserve different directory boundaries

sections.heading: Trust is not synchronization
sections.text: One-way or two-way supported external/forest trusts allow authentication across directory boundaries. Trust direction defines which domain's users can access the other domain's resources; it does not copy every user.

sections.heading: Prepare the hybrid path
sections.text: DX/VPN routing, DNS forwarding, required ports and compatible directory configuration must work before a trust can be used. Verify both authentication and application authorization.

sections.heading: Replicate where required
sections.text: A self-managed domain-controller replica on EC2 can keep that existing domain closer to workloads. Operate its replication and recovery yourself; an AD Connector alone cannot remove a WAN authentication dependency.

repairs.remember: A trust links domains; replication copies directory state within its supported model.
repairs.layout: Module09 style; named teaching sections with clean functional service illustrations

repairs.title: STS APIs create different kinds of temporary sessions

sections.heading: Assume a role
sections.text: AssumeRole creates a role session within an account or across accounts. The role trust policy, caller authorization and session restrictions must support the request.

sections.heading: Federate with an identity token
sections.text: AssumeRoleWithSAML accepts an eligible SAML assertion; AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity accepts a supported OIDC/web identity token. Validate issuer, audience and subject instead of trusting a token solely because it is signed.

sections.heading: User and broker sessions
sections.text: GetSessionToken supplies an eligible IAM user's temporary credentials, including supported MFA context. GetFederationToken supports a broker-created federated-user session with its own scoped authorization behavior.

repairs.remember: Temporary credentials are not interchangeable: identify which API and principal created the session.
repairs.layout: Module09 style; named teaching sections with clean functional service illustrations

repairs.title: Policy conditions: choose the operator and context key

sections.heading: Match the value's type
sections.text: StringEquals/StringLike, numeric, date, Bool, IP-address and ARN operators solve different comparisons. Conditions inspect request context; keys are not present for every caller or network path.

sections.heading: Use variables deliberately
sections.text: Supported variables can scope a resource or condition to context such as a principal tag or username. A variable that fits an IAM user may not exist for an assumed-role session.

sections.heading: Test missing context
sections.text: Null checks key presence; IfExists and negated operators alter missing-key behavior. Test both an expected request and a request without the key before using the condition as a security boundary.

repairs.remember: An operator, a context key and missing-key behavior together define the condition.
repairs.layout: Module09 style; named teaching sections with clean functional service illustrations

repairs.title: Tag set operators do not automatically require every tag

sections.heading: Compare request values
sections.text: ForAllValues tests every supplied request value against allowed policy values; ForAnyValue tests whether at least one matches. Use set operators only with supported multivalued context keys such as aws:TagKeys.

sections.heading: Require the keys separately
sections.text: ForAllValues can match when the key is missing. Combine an appropriate presence check with explicit requirements for each required aws:RequestTag key; an allowed-key list alone does not prove every required tag was submitted.

sections.heading: Protect the tag lifecycle
sections.text: Control tag creation, updates and deletion as well as resource creation. Restrict which principals can change security-relevant principal/resource tags used by ABAC.

repairs.remember: Allowed tag names, required tag presence and permission to change tags are separate controls.
repairs.layout: Module09 style; named teaching sections with clean functional service illustrations

repairs.title: Managed policies: broad access is not an explicit deny

sections.heading: AdministratorAccess
sections.text: A broad identity-policy allow still operates inside applicable organization guardrails, resource controls and explicit denies. AdministratorAccess does not bypass every authorization boundary.

sections.heading: PowerUserAccess
sections.text: This AWS-managed policy allows broad service use while excluding broad identity/account administration, with specific exceptions defined by its current version. Inspect the live policy rather than memorizing a frozen exception list.

sections.heading: NotAction is a selection
sections.text: NotAction selects actions outside the named set for that statement; it is not itself an explicit Deny. Other policies and the statement's Effect still determine the effective result.

repairs.remember: Read Effect, action selection and all applicable boundaries together.
repairs.layout: Module09 style; named teaching sections with clean functional service illustrations

repairs.title: VPC endpoint policy: an additional authorization filter

sections.heading: Constrain the endpoint path
sections.text: A supported endpoint policy limits eligible principals, actions or resources for requests through that endpoint. It does not supply a network route, replace service authorization or govern requests that use another path.

sections.heading: Evaluate applicable policies
sections.text: The caller and resource must satisfy the relevant authorization rules. A same-account resource policy can sometimes supply the allow directly; do not assume every allowed request requires an identity-policy allow.

sections.heading: Enforce the intended boundary
sections.text: Use supported resource-policy conditions and network design when access must use a particular endpoint. Explicit denies and applicable SCPs/RCPs, boundaries and session policies still matter.

repairs.remember: Endpoint reachability, endpoint filtering and service authorization are different checks.
repairs.layout: Module09 style; named teaching sections with clean functional service illustrations

repairs.title: Created, invited and moved accounts have different setup steps

sections.heading: Created member account
sections.text: Organizations normally creates OrganizationAccountAccessRole for a newly created member account. Authorized management-account principals can assume it; the trust and IAM permissions still matter.

sections.heading: Invited existing account
sections.text: The same administrator role is not automatically created for an invited account. Review existing access, logs, controls and costs before onboarding; establish a deliberate administration model.

sections.heading: Move between organizations
sections.text: Meet account-removal prerequisites, leave/remove the old organization, then invite and accept into the new one. Recheck effective policies, service integrations and billing; changing an OU is a different operation.

repairs.remember: Account membership does not automatically create every administrative or service integration.
repairs.layout: Module09 style; named teaching sections with clean functional service illustrations

repairs.title: Organizations: billing benefits and governance features

sections.heading: Understand the feature set
sections.text: Consolidated billing aggregates eligible account usage and payment. All features adds supported organization governance capabilities; enabling it can require invited-account approval and is not a reversible downgrade to billing-only.

sections.heading: Share discounts deliberately
sections.text: Management-account settings control eligible Reserved Instance and Savings Plans discount sharing. Check current billing rules and sharing settings for participating accounts.

sections.heading: Keep boundaries separate
sections.text: A shared billing discount does not grant IAM access to another account's resources or transfer ownership. Capacity-reservation behavior and resource quotas require their own design.

repairs.remember: Consolidated billing is a financial relationship; governance and authorization add separate controls.
repairs.layout: Module09 style; named teaching sections with clean functional service illustrations

repairs.title: Tag policies standardize; creation controls require presence

sections.heading: Standardize the taxonomy
sections.text: Organizations tag policies define supported tag keys, capitalization and allowed values, and can enforce supported tagging operations or report compliance.

sections.heading: Require important tags
sections.text: A tag policy alone does not force every resource to have every required tag. Use appropriate service/IAM/SCP request-tag conditions and supported provisioning controls for mandatory tagging.

sections.heading: Use the result responsibly
sections.text: Cost-allocation reporting and ABAC depend on meaningful tags and controlled tag mutation. Test untagged resources, unsupported services and permitted exceptions.

repairs.remember: Tag compliance, mandatory presence and tag-based authorization are related but different jobs.
repairs.layout: Module09 style; named teaching sections with clean functional service illustrations

repairs.title: Organization policies: data-use preferences and backup plans

sections.heading: Scope AI data-use preferences
sections.text: AI services opt-out policies govern supported services and the organization scope to which they apply. Verify each service's current data-use terms; do not treat one policy as a universal rule for all AI products.

sections.heading: Define centralized backup intent
sections.text: Organizations backup policies define supported backup-plan behavior such as schedules, windows, selections and copy requirements through inherited effective policies.

sections.heading: Prove execution
sections.text: A policy is not evidence that resources were selected, a role had permissions or a backup succeeded. Check effective plans, resource eligibility, job results and restore tests; retain local operational ownership.

repairs.remember: An inherited policy expresses intent; service evidence proves that intent was executed.
repairs.layout: Module09 style; named teaching sections with clean functional service illustrations

repairs.title: Parameter hierarchy is also an authorization boundary

sections.heading: Organize configuration
sections.text: Use meaningful paths such as /prod/payments/endpoint and versioned parameter values. Supported public parameters and Secrets Manager references have different ownership and access behavior.

sections.heading: Control recursive reads
sections.text: GetParametersByPath can expose descendants of an authorized path. Review recursive access carefully; a broad parent-path permission can undermine a design that assumes child-path isolation.

sections.heading: Authorize decrypted values
sections.text: SecureString uses KMS and appropriate decrypt authorization. IAM access, KMS permissions, version selection and application caching all affect which configuration the application actually sees.

repairs.remember: A convenient parent path must not become an accidental cross-environment read permission.
repairs.layout: Module09 style; named teaching sections with clean functional service illustrations

repairs.title: Parameter Store tiers and policies solve separate problems

sections.heading: Choose storage attributes
sections.text: Standard supports smaller values and a lower parameter count; Advanced supports larger values, more parameters, parameter policies and supported sharing at additional cost. Tier and API throughput are different controls.

sections.heading: Name the policy behavior
sections.text: Expiration deletes at the configured time; ExpirationNotification and NoChangeNotification publish supported notifications. A notification does not rotate the external credential by itself.

sections.heading: Plan the lifecycle
sections.text: Standard can be upgraded; Advanced cannot be downgraded in place. Inspect the current tier limits and costs, retain needed values and build any rotation/update workflow explicitly.

repairs.remember: Parameter expiration, change notification and secret rotation are different mechanisms.
repairs.layout: Module09 style; named teaching sections with clean functional service illustrations

repairs.title: CloudFormation secret references are not a rotation engine

sections.heading: Generate or reference a secret
sections.text: A template can create a Secrets Manager secret and reference its value without embedding plaintext credentials in the template. Grant the deployment and consuming services only the required access.

sections.heading: Separate deployment from rotation
sections.text: Updating only the secret value does not automatically refresh a resource property containing a dynamic reference. CloudFormation resolves it during the relevant create/update operation.

sections.heading: Keep consumers current
sections.text: Configure an appropriate rotation workflow and consumer refresh strategy. Existing environment variables, connections and application caches may retain older values until refreshed or restarted.

repairs.remember: A dynamic reference avoids plaintext templates; rotation and consumer refresh still need design.
repairs.layout: Module09 style; named teaching sections with clean functional service illustrations

repairs.title: Cross-account secret reads must pass three authorization gates

sections.heading: Caller identity permission
sections.text: The consuming account's principal needs appropriate secretsmanager:GetSecretValue permission for the intended secret ARN and context.

sections.heading: Secret resource policy
sections.text: The secret owner must grant the intended external principal access through a supported resource-based policy. Scope principals and conditions; avoid unintended external sharing.

sections.heading: Customer-managed KMS key
sections.text: For a secret encrypted with the owner's customer-managed key, permit the consumer's required decrypt use in applicable key/IAM policies. A secret permission alone does not authorize its encryption key.

repairs.remember: Cross-account access needs permission to the secret and permission to use its key.
repairs.layout: Module09 style; named teaching sections with clean functional service illustrations

repairs.title: KMS key material origin is different from key ownership

sections.heading: AWS-generated or imported
sections.text: A customer-managed key can use AWS-generated material or supported imported material. Imported-material expiry, deletion and reimport behavior require an explicit availability and recovery plan.

sections.heading: CloudHSM custom key store
sections.text: A supported custom key store backs KMS operations with a connected CloudHSM cluster. KMS integration remains, while cluster availability, capacity and operations become dependencies.

sections.heading: External key store
sections.text: An external key store delegates supported cryptographic operations to an external key manager through its proxy. This is different from importing material into KMS; latency and external outages affect AWS workloads.

repairs.remember: Ownership, material origin and the location performing cryptographic operations are separate decisions.
repairs.layout: Module09 style; named teaching sections with clean functional service illustrations

repairs.title: NAT instances: operate the forwarding host deliberately

sections.heading: Configure the complete path
sections.text: A NAT instance is an EC2 forwarding host in a suitable public subnet. Configure its public/EIP path, forwarding software and private-subnet route, and disable source/destination checking as required.

sections.heading: Own the failure handling
sections.text: Instance bandwidth, security configuration, patching, scaling and failover are your responsibility. A single forwarding host is a single failure domain.

sections.heading: Compare managed egress
sections.text: Use an appropriate managed NAT design when it meets the workload requirements. Do not infer that a legacy NAT-instance example supplies managed availability or automatic scaling.

repairs.remember: A route to a forwarding instance works only when the host and the return path work too.
repairs.layout: Module09 style; named teaching sections with clean functional service illustrations

repairs.title: Flow Logs: inspect the fields and the observation point

sections.heading: Read the flow record
sections.text: Interface, source/destination addresses, ports, protocol, packets, bytes, timestamps, action and log status describe an aggregated observed flow, not the application payload.

sections.heading: Interpret NAT correctly
sections.text: At middlebox or NAT interfaces, srcaddr/dstaddr can reflect the observation point. Supported packet-level fields such as pkt-srcaddr/pkt-dstaddr help distinguish original packet addresses.

sections.heading: Avoid false conclusions
sections.text: ACCEPT or REJECT is evidence, not a complete root cause. Correlate both directions, security controls, routes and application logs; some traffic is excluded and records can be delayed or skipped.

repairs.remember: The ENI, field definition and collection scope determine what a flow-log record proves.
repairs.layout: Module09 style; named teaching sections with clean functional service illustrations

repairs.title: IP-based routing and geoproximity answer different questions

sections.heading: Route by client CIDR
sections.text: IP-based records use CIDR collections and location mappings for known client network ranges. Configure the supported unmatched-location behavior and consider DNS resolver/client-subnet visibility.

sections.heading: Shift geographic catchments
sections.text: Geoproximity uses resource/user location and a bias to expand or shrink the area served by an endpoint. It is different from country-based geolocation and measured-latency routing.

sections.heading: Choose the control surface
sections.text: Current geoproximity records can be configured directly where supported; Traffic Flow is useful for complex reusable policies. Do not repeat the older claim that every geoproximity configuration requires Traffic Flow.

repairs.remember: Client networks, user geography and measured latency are different routing inputs.
repairs.layout: Module09 style; named teaching sections with clean functional service illustrations

repairs.title: Health checks: endpoint probes, aggregation and private signals

sections.heading: Check a public endpoint
sections.text: HTTP/HTTPS checks evaluate configured response criteria; TCP checks test connection behavior. Allow checker traffic, use the intended hostname/path, and validate optional response-string matching.

sections.heading: Combine health evidence
sections.text: Calculated checks combine child results using configured thresholds or logical rules. Checker aggregation and calculated-child limits are separate controls; consult current API/console limits.

sections.heading: Monitor private readiness
sections.text: Public health checkers cannot directly reach private endpoints. Use supported CloudWatch metric/alarm health signals and a prepared failover target; changing an alarm's display state is not a substitute for its metric data.

repairs.remember: A health check must measure the failure your routing policy is intended to handle.
repairs.layout: Module09 style; named teaching sections with clean functional service illustrations

repairs.title: Traffic Flow and DNS caching make controlled changes repeatable

sections.heading: Build reusable routing logic
sections.text: Traffic Flow represents complex decision trees as versioned traffic policies and policy instances. A policy definition and the DNS records created from it are different resources.

sections.heading: Test geographic and weighted decisions
sections.text: Bias changes catchment size, while weights influence DNS-answer selection. Neither guarantees an exact share of individual HTTP requests because resolvers and clients cache answers.

sections.heading: Plan rollout and rollback
sections.text: Review TTL, record scope, health behavior, cost and the fallback for all-unhealthy or unmatched locations. Validate authoritative answers and client behavior before broad rollout.

repairs.remember: Version the routing decision and test the cached client path, not just the policy editor.
repairs.layout: Module09 style; named teaching sections with clean functional service illustrations

repairs.title: Multi-Region Access Points: global entry and regional data

sections.heading: Use a global access path
sections.text: An S3 Multi-Region Access Point presents a global endpoint over configured regional buckets and routes supported requests using its service behavior. It does not make every object's data appear in every bucket.

sections.heading: Replicate and authorize separately
sections.text: Configure supported replication, bucket/MRAP policies, ownership and encryption-key access for the intended requests. Version and replication state still determine which regional data exists.

sections.heading: Control regional failover
sections.text: Failover controls adjust eligible regional request routing. Prepare destination data and permissions before shifting traffic; a routing change alone is not a complete disaster-recovery plan.

repairs.remember: Global request routing and regional object replication are separate mechanisms.
repairs.layout: Module09 style; named teaching sections with clean functional service illustrations

repairs.title: Legacy S3 transforms and Glacier vault retention need context

sections.heading: Understand Object Lambda
sections.text: The historical Object Lambda pattern transformed supported object responses through Lambda. Availability is now restricted to existing customers and selected partner use; verify eligibility before designing a new workload.

sections.heading: Choose a current transform path
sections.text: For new designs, evaluate an appropriate application/Lambda/API or CloudFront processing path. Transform authorization, caching and latency still need explicit design.

sections.heading: Separate Glacier Vault Lock
sections.text: Glacier vault-service retention policies belong to the historical vault API model. They are different from S3 Object Lock on versioned bucket objects and from selecting an S3 Glacier storage class.

repairs.remember: Preserve the old exam concept while selecting a supported current service model.
repairs.layout: Module09 style; named teaching sections with clean functional service illustrations

repairs.title: Presigned URLs delegate a bounded request

sections.heading: Authorize the signer
sections.text: A presigned URL represents a particular signed request using the signer's permissions. Scope the operation, bucket/key and required request headers; possession of the URL can grant the intended bearer access.

sections.heading: Bound the lifetime
sections.text: The URL's expiry cannot outlive the usable signing credentials and may be constrained further by policy. Temporary role credentials can expire before a requested URL lifetime.

sections.heading: Protect the workflow
sections.text: Use HTTPS, controlled distribution and appropriate object/size/checksum conditions for the chosen upload mechanism. Test failures and avoid exposing long-lived credentials to the client.

repairs.remember: A presigned URL is delegated request authority, not a new public bucket policy.
repairs.layout: Module09 style; named teaching sections with clean functional service illustrations

repairs.title: S3 evidence: access logs, data events and metrics

sections.heading: Server access logs
sections.text: Access logging records supported request details to a configured destination. Treat delivery and coverage characteristics as part of the evidence model; it is not a real-time application tracing guarantee.

sections.heading: CloudTrail data events
sections.text: Configure relevant S3 object-level data-event selectors when object API audit is required. Management-event history alone does not automatically record every object read or write.

sections.heading: Operational metrics
sections.text: Request metrics and Storage Lens show aggregate signals at their supported scope and cadence. A metric, an access log and an API audit event answer different questions.

repairs.remember: Choose evidence by the question: which API, which request, or what aggregate trend?
repairs.layout: Module09 style; named teaching sections with clean functional service illustrations
